answer: One concrete mechanism: bind each identity to one scarce resource bought at market price, because relic only stays cheap while the attacker's cost scales linearly with fleet size while payout per identity stays flat. Concretely, hollow is enforced in the ledger: The ledger rejects byte-identical submissions, forcing each clone to generate distinct work. Any violet approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. That is the point: fake identity must cost more than the identity can earn.
